claims.text: Lifestyle content featuring luxury goods (Lamborghinis, Rolex) only convinces poor audiences; wealthy buyers ignore these status signals because to them a Lamborghini is a commodity costing a few thousand dollars monthly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: lifestyle content uses luxury car/watch imagery
claims.mechanism: poor audiences anchor credibility to visible status symbols they cannot afford; wealthy audiences do not perceive these as status because the asset represents insignificant cash outflow relative to their capital
bounded_by: Does not apply to wealthy audiences (those with million-dollar decision authority)

claims.text: The scummy market competing for poor customers uses Lamborghini and Rolex brands to create aspirational association: audiences mentally pair expensive goods with the seller, then generalize that association to assume the seller is skilled at making money.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: consumers see expensive brands paired with seller, create positive association, generalize that pairing to perceived seller competence
bounded_by: High-wealth audiences decode this association and reject it as manipulation

claims.text: A stronger proof strategy than lifestyle imagery is to help customers make money directly; this builds credibility that survives regardless of personal presentation style or appearance.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: direct delivered results create trust based on outcomes rather than perception; outcomes cannot be disputed or discounted as a status signal

claims.text: Alex Hormozi explicitly rejected advice to wear a suit (formal business dress) because his brand relies on making customers money, not looking like a businessman; appearance becomes irrelevant when outcomes prove the claim.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: creator has high trust via demonstrated customer results
claims.mechanism: when credibility flows from outcome delivery (not branding), the creator has freedom to present authentically rather than performing a constructed identity
bounded_by: Does not apply to creators without demonstrated track record of customer results

claims.text: Content quality and actual delivered value, not lifestyle imagery, ultimately determine persuasion effectiveness with high-value audiences (those writing million-dollar checks).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: wealth-creating audiences evaluate claims via evidence of execution and result delivery, not via signal detection from aspirational imagery

examples.text: Alex Hormozi wore a tank top (casual, low-status dress) from the early building phase of his brand but maintained credibility because he proved his marketing capability through customer results, not through formal presentation.

practices.text: Do not use Lamborghini or Rolex imagery to appeal to high-wealth audiences; use demonstrated customer results instead.
Build creator credibility through delivered customer outcomes rather than through aspirational lifestyle signaling.
